question: Does the committed random-yardstick comparison use the matched-pair observed medians?
answer: NO — the committed 'observed' statistics (0.820 / 0.7715) are medians over all 5,460 unordered pairs of the 105 countries, while the random draws use their 52 pairs. The matched-pair medians are 0.620 / 0.2375; against those the shares are 96.1% / 100.0%, i.e. the matched pairs are LESS divergent than random pairing (direction of the paper's point survives; the magnitude and the 'central honest null' sentence do not).
reproduction: python3 scripts/erratum_check_q2_yardstick.py (this record; reads data/long_run_panel.csv and results/audit/pairs_primary.csv; same algorithm and seed as scripts/q2_audit.py)
